title: TS-12 Members CLI and first-org seed
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 12 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 12); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Port the members command line tool and the first-organization seed to TypeScript.

## Kind
mechanical-port: the Python source below is the specification. Keep its structure, names (camelCase), branches and messages. Do not redesign anything.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/12-members-cli-and-first-org-seed origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): members CLI and first-org seed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/12-members-cli-and-first-org-seed
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/bin/members.ts`
- `conversation/src/members/cli.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/members-cli.steps.ts`
- `conversation/features-support/steps/first-org-seed.steps.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
`runMembersCli(argv: string[], deps): Promise<{exitCode: number; stdout: string; stderr: string}>`; sub-commands, flags and output text are identical to the Python CLI (copy the help text).

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Python source to port (keep structure; read it fully before writing)
- `python/src/chatticus/members/__main__.py (327 lines; port in two commits)`
Rule: mechanical ports keep the Python file's structure and cite the Python line range in the commit body. Behavior that no scenario encodes is still kept.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

### features/members_cli.feature
Scenarios: List pending organizations then enable without a computer; Suspend then reinstate via the members CLI with confirmation
Step texts to implement in TypeScript (exact step text, then the Python step that implements it today):
```text
an empty organization records store   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:40
"ryan@example.com" has signed in   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:63
that user has created organization "Anthus Labs"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:77
the members CLI lists organizations with status "pending"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:13
the members CLI output includes organization "Anthus Labs"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:64
the members CLI enables organization "Anthus Labs" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:25
organization "Anthus Labs" has status "enabled"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:297
no computer exists for "Anthus Labs"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:380
the members CLI suspends organization "Anthus Labs" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:38
the members CLI lists organizations with status "suspended"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:13
the members CLI reinstates organization "Anthus Labs" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:51
```

### features/first_org_seed.feature
Scenarios: Cold path creates a pending organization then enables without a computer; Anthus backfill preserves existing messaging rows; A different email is not an owner of seeded anthus; Cold path seeds anthus enabled with Anthus AI Solutions on empty store
Step texts to implement in TypeScript (exact step text, then the Python step that implements it today):
```text
an empty organization records store   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:40
the members CLI creates organization "Bootstrap Labs" for owner "owner@example.com"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:44
organization "Bootstrap Labs" has status "pending"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:297
the members CLI lists organizations with status "pending"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:13
the members CLI output includes organization "Bootstrap Labs"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:64
the members CLI enables organization "Bootstrap Labs" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:25
organization "Bootstrap Labs" has status "enabled"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:297
no computer exists for "Bootstrap Labs"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:380
a messaging store with tenant "anthus" user "ryan" bot data and no organization records   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:18
the members CLI seeds tenant "anthus" for owner "owner@example.com" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:71
organization tenant "anthus" has status "enabled"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:111
an identity exists for "owner@example.com"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:284
"owner@example.com" is an owner member of tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:132
tenant "anthus" user "ryan" bot data still exists   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:148
no computer exists for tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:155
the members CLI seeds tenant "anthus" for owner "owner@example.com" with confirmation again   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:74
"other@example.com" signs in   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:55
"other@example.com" is not a member of tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:141
the members CLI seeds tenant "anthus" for owner "ryan@anth.us" named "Anthus AI Solutions" with confirmation   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:71
organization tenant "anthus" has display name "Anthus AI Solutions"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:117
an identity exists for "ryan@anth.us"   <-  features/steps/organization_steps.py:284
the identity for "ryan@anth.us" is keyed in lowercase   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:123
"ryan@anth.us" is an owner member of tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py:132
the members CLI lists organizations with status "enabled"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:13
the members CLI output includes tenant "anthus"   <-  features/steps/members_cli_steps.py:72
```
Cucumber expressions: convert each Python `{name}` parse pattern to `{string}`, `{int}` or `{word}` using `npx tsx conversation/bin/convert-step-pattern.ts '<pattern>'` (from ticket 3) and review the output by hand. Step text must not change unless behavior changed. Steps call `this.api` (HTTP via `app.request()`) for HTTP steps and the same domain functions the routes call for direct steps; steps never reach into a store.
Step file(s) to write: under `conversation/features-support/steps/` as named in Files above (at most about 400 lines each; split by subject).

Failing run first (required):
```text
1. Write or port the step file(s) and any new .feature file.
2. cd conversation && npx cucumber-js ../features/<feature>.feature   -> confirm the scenarios FAIL for the right reason (missing production code, not a typo in a step). Save the first failing summary line for the commit body.
3. Write the smallest production code that passes. Re-run until green.
```
Manifest: when EVERY scenario of a feature is covered by this ticket (not marked partial above), add `features/<name>.feature` to `features/ported-features.txt` and add `<name>` to the alternation in `python/behave.ini` `exclude_re` (the manifest vitest `conversation/test/ported-features-manifest.test.ts` fails if they disagree). For a partial feature leave the manifest alone; the ticket named in the note finishes it. To run a partial feature, pass the path and `--name '<scenario>'` to cucumber-js; if CLI paths do not override the config paths, stop and report.

## Dependencies (blocked-by)
- ticket 8 (chatticus-4b67bc): Organizations, membership and identity kernel; provides what its Files section lists.

## Verify
```text
cd conversation && npm run typecheck && npm test && npx cucumber-js ../features/<each feature of this ticket>.feature
```
moto setup (copied from the `conversation` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml):
```text
python -m pip install "moto[server]==5.2.3"
nohup moto_server -p 5555 > moto.log 2>&1 &
for i in $(seq 1 30); do if (echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/5555) 2>/dev/null; then break; fi; sleep 1; done
export CHATTICUS_TEST_AWS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:5555
```
Install once at the repo root: `npm ci`. Stop moto when done: `pkill -f "moto_server -p 5555"`.
If the ticket added a feature to the manifest also run `cd conversation && npx cucumber-js` (full manifest) and `cd python && behave` is NOT required for ported features, but run `cd python && black --check src ../features tests && ruff check src ../features tests` if you touched anything under python/ or features/steps/.
Final cleanup before pushing:
```text
git status
```
Make sure NO `.orig`, `.rej`, `node_modules`, `build/`, `dist/`, `moto.log`, `.venv` or other stray files are staged: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E '\.orig$|\.rej$|node_modules|(^|/)build/|(^|/)dist/|moto\.log|\.venv'` must print nothing.

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation. Never improvise, never weaken or delete a scenario to make it pass, never add a fallback or a compatibility branch.

## Python to delete
No production Python is deleted by this ticket (the one big deletion is ticket 40). The only deletions allowed: the per-feature step file of each feature newly added to the manifest, because the manifest vitest requires it: features/steps/members_cli_steps.py (if it exists), features/steps/first_org_seed_steps.py (if it exists). Shared step files (control_plane_steps.py, capability_policy_steps.py, messaging_steps.py, organization_steps.py and the like) are never edited here; the last ticket that uses them leaves them for ticket 40.
